ph: Deputy Mayor, Mr. Abdul Latif, offering the -Key to the City

w: In the evening Satsang assembly in San Jose, Lord Harikrishna Maharaj was honored by the devotees.

At 8.50 pm Swamishri arrived in the assembly held in a huge marquee. A replica of Dada Khachar’s darbar formed the stage backdrop with the marble murtis of Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, Ghanshyam Maharaj, Harikrishna Maharaj (metal), Radha-Krishna Dev, Sita-Ram and Hanumanji, Shiv-Parvatiji and Ganpatiji and Guru Parampara. The Brahmin pundits, Shri Ghanshyambhai Shukla and Mukeshbhai, were conducting the pratishtha rituals. The initial rituals had been completed by the senior sadhus: Tyagvallabh Swami, Ishwarcharan Swami and Viveksagar Swami. Swamishri performed the final rituals before Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj by ‘opening the eyes’, invoking the Divine, holding a mirror and performing pujan of all the murtis. After the annakut was arranged Swamishri performed the pratishtha arti and mantra pushpanjali. Finally Swamishri blessed the congregation and praised the faith, patience and unity of the devotees of LA. Then the devotees honoured Swamishri’s Shri Harikrishna Maharaj. A nagar yatra of the murtis was carried out in the mandir precincts. The murtis were arranged on golf carts with children, teenagers, youths dressed in traditional dresses and dancing to the celebration tunes, bhajans. Sadhus and devotees joined the procession, singing dhun and bhajan. At the rear of the nagar yatra women devotees in traditional dress were singing dhun and bhajan. The murtis were then established in the Haveli foyer for darshan. The next day (16/9) Swamishri performed the rituals of the first stone-laying ceremony on the mandir kanpeeth. In the evening, children and volunteers presented a Children’s Day programme themed ‘Educational Excellence’. The invited guests were honoured: Congressman Gary Miller, Protem Mayor of Chino Hills Mr Hagman, Former Mayor of Chino Hills Mr Ed Graham, Council Member of Chino Hills Mr Bill Krueger, Orange County Superior Court Judge Mr James Gray, Planning Commissioners of Chino Hills Mr Art Bennett and Mr Adam, Engineer and Developer Mr Jan Dabrey and President of Chino Hills Medical Center Mr James Lally.

The famous Sindhi industrialist Harubhai Mahtani, who had come from Indonesia, brought his grandson (his daughter's son). He said, "Last year on Guru Purnima I came for your darshan with my grandson, and you said to him, 'Do not eat meat, remain vegetarian.' It has been a year since then, and he has not touched meat."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj was pleased to hear this. Everyone experienced how powerful Swamishri's words are, even on a child who was completely new to the spiritual path.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj was pleased to hear this. Everyone experienced how much influence Swamishri's words have even on a child who is entirely new to seeking.

As Mahant Swami Maharaj was coming down the steps, he was meeting the craftsmen doing seva on the Akshardham mandir with folded hands through his glance. Halfway down he stopped. Turning back, he said, "Those up there were left out of my glance." Then, standing right there, he lovingly met each craftsman one by one through his glance.

Yesterday Swamishri had noticed that one sadhu had been left out when giving prasad, and today that some craftsmen had been left out of receiving his glance. In Swamishri's mind, no one should be left out of anything.
Mahant Swami Maharaj came to the ongoing shibir session, in which a question and answer session with Swamishri began.
Question: You have written about Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "The real sadhu." What did you see in Pramukh Swami Maharaj that made you write "the real sadhu"?

Swamishri said, "When I first met Pramukh Swami Maharaj, I had not read the Vachanamrut or Swami ni Vato, but my heart accepted that this is the real sadhu. His expressions, his alertness, his innocence were such that one immediately felt that this is the real sadhu."
Question: In the morning katha you said that we do not take what Pramukh Swami Maharaj wants to give. So what does he want to give us?

Swamishri said, "He wants to give only Akshardham, nothing else. Whatever he does or has done is for that. We feel that Swami gave blessings for a house, but it was not for that; he gave blessings for a house in Akshardham. Like the fly that comes along with the ox."
Question: As you have said, Swami Bapa kept a respectful reserve with you. So how did you experience his love in that?
Swamishri said, "I used to feel supreme peace. I felt steady." Then, remembering Swami Bapa, he said, "He would put his hand on everyone's head, but when I came, he would not."
Question: What thought came to you when you were installed as guru?
Swamishri said, "Whatever they (Maharaj and Swami) want to do, they will do."
At the end, Vivekmurtidas Swami prayed, "There may be some shortcoming in how we ask, but please accept it and take us to Akshardham."
Swamishri said, "It is Shriji Maharaj's promise. They have come only to take us to Akshardham."
This last sentence says a great deal.

The attendant sadhus put their dilemma before Mahant Swami Maharaj: everyone wishes, "Please turn our malas. But more than 50 malas come in a day; how is it possible for you to turn every one of them and sanctify them? So we have you touch them and give them back. Then by that touch, can the mala be said to be as sanctified as if you had turned it, or not?"
Swamishri said, "By touch and by glance, it is even more than if I had turned it."
Swamishri's power can never be bound by any limit. He can sanctify anything in any way, because he is all pervading.
Mahant Swami Maharaj came to the assembly. Now the programme under the shibir began: "Iti Vachanamrutam."
Just as questions and answers took place with Shriji Maharaj in the Vachanamrut, in the same way a series of questions and answers went on with Swamishri.
Question: "Swami! I take your photo, and a photo of Shriji Maharaj or Pramukh Swami Maharaj comes out instead. Why is this?"
Swamishri said emphatically, "It is he."
There was tremendous applause.
Question: "Shriji Maharaj has given the boon of coming to take us at the end of life, but we have never seen Shriji Maharaj, so when he comes at the end, how will we recognise him?"
Swamishri said, "When there is knowledge, you will recognise him. Whatever form he comes in, one who has knowledge and firm conviction will recognise him at once."

In answer to a question after that, Swamishri spoke greatly about the glory of the "Satsang Shikshan Pariksha" (satsang education examinations). Hearing this, the presenter said, "Hearing Swamishri say this, everyone has resolved to take the Satsang Shikshan Pariksha."
Swamishri immediately shook his head to say no. Seeing this, everyone raised a finger to show they were ready to take the exams.
Swamishri asked, "Will you prepare and take them?"
Everyone said yes together in a loud voice. This way of Swamishri's of inspiring everyone to take the Satsang Shikshan Pariksha was wonderful.

In the next question a short dialogue was presented. One volunteer said, "From today, arti, Vachanamrut and Swami ni Vato are stopped." The other volunteer asked, "Why?" And the first volunteer said, "Shriji Maharaj has said in the Vachanamrut that singing without remembrance is as good as not singing, so why not just stop?"
Swamishri was told, "Swami! Many people have this question. For one thing, we do not understand, and also, while doing all this, we do not keep remembrance. So what should we do?"

Answering, Swamishri said, "Someone said to Yogi Bapa, 'Shriji Maharaj has said that an ekadashi (fast) is true if the mind stays under control, but the mind does not stay under control and it becomes a cattle fast.' A cattle fast means you have the desire but do not get the food. So he said, 'Instead, why not just eat?' Yogi Bapa said, 'No. Do not eat at all. Keep the ekadashi. Even if you do not get 100 percent, take whatever percent you get, 50, 20 or 15.' We should do the same in everything. As in Vachanamrut Gadhada I 22, keep doing it even if the mind does not stay focused. By doing it like this, we will progress. Otherwise, by slipping and slipping, we will slip away completely."
